title: Kestrel Closed-End Consumer Lease Money Factor and Residual Sheet
content:
**Kestrel Closed-End Consumer Lease — base money factors, residual percentages and contractable mileage**

The base money factor of a Kestrel Closed-End Consumer Lease depends on the tier and on the term band into which the lease term falls. A dealer may add a markup to the base money factor of no more than 0.0004 in every tier.

| Tier | Terms of 24 to 36 months | Terms of 37 to 39 months | Terms of 40 to 48 months | Maximum dealer markup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Kestrel Lease Tier 5 | 0.00310 | 0.00315 | 0.00325 | 0.0004 |
| Kestrel Lease Tier 4 | 0.00265 | 0.00270 | 0.00280 | 0.0004 |
| Kestrel Lease Tier 3 | 0.00225 | 0.00230 | 0.00240 | 0.0004 |
| Kestrel Lease Tier 2 | 0.00195 | 0.00200 | 0.00210 | 0.0004 |
| Kestrel Lease Tier 1 | 0.00170 | 0.00175 | 0.00185 | 0.0004 |
| Kestrel Lease Tier 1+ | 0.00150 | 0.00155 | 0.00165 | 0.0004 |

**Residual value percentages (all six tiers alike)**

The residual percentage of MSRP is set by the lease term and stated at the 12000-mile annual allowance:

| Lease term | 24 months | 36 months | 39 months | 48 months |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Residual, percent of MSRP | 66 | 58 | 56 | 49 |

The contracted annual mileage allowance then adds percentage points to that residual percentage:

| Annual mileage allowance | 10000 miles | 12000 miles | 15000 miles |
|---|---|---|---|
| Points added to the residual percent | plus 1 | 0 | minus 3 |

**Contractable allowances**: only 10000, 12000 or 15000 miles a year may be contracted, in every tier.

**Worked illustration (hypothetical figures)**: a 36-month lease at a 15000-mile allowance carries a residual of 58 less 3, that is 55 percent of MSRP; on a hypothetical MSRP of $40000 that is $22000. The same lease in Kestrel Lease Tier 2 starts from a base money factor of 0.00195, to which the dealer may add up to 0.0004.
